C1.name: Generated completeness claims
C1.rule: No generated text may claim completeness (e.g. 'complete evidence base', 'not a search gap', 'every eligible trial', 'no eligible trial is missing') unless the search is recorded as systematic (the review object's search / search_completeness state says so). 'Population match' must be computed per axis (each PICO axis separately), never asserted as one verdict. The comparator's method type must come from its own text/object, not be inferred.
C1.seen: External audit review 15 (semaglutide-obesity-mace): generated completeness wording on a known-item search; population match asserted as a whole.

C2.name: Comparator 'same question' asserted, not derived
C2.rule: The comparator panel's 'Scope match (is this the same question?)' verdict ('same question' / 'SCOPE MISMATCH') must be generated from the comparator's own PICO object compared axis by axis with ours (population, intervention level, comparator, outcome, design), and must not say 'same question' when any axis differs or is unknown.
C2.seen: Review 22 (tranexamic-acid-pph) and audit fix A2 (colchicine-recurrent-pericarditis): a 2012 meta was labelled 'the same question' while broader in population and design.

C3.name: k=1 pooling wording
C3.rule: An outcome served from ONE trial (k=1) must never be described as pooled, nor as 'pooled by PM/HKSJ', 'random-effects', 'Paule-Mandel', 'HKSJ', heterogeneity, or a prediction interval. Reported and reconstructed single-trial estimates must say which they are.
C3.seen: Review 15 (semaglutide-obesity-mace) and earlier H13/H19: method text that describes PM/HKSJ pooling on a single-trial outcome.

C4.name: Leave-one-out display without intervals
C4.rule: The leave-one-out sensitivity shows only point estimates ('every LOO estimate ... no single trial drives it'). Each LOO row must show its HKSJ 95% CI (computed by the SAME canonical pooling path), and the text must separate point stability from inference stability (e.g. every LOO CI crosses the null). Words like 'robust' or 'no single trial drives it' must not be emitted when an LOO CI changes the inference.
C4.seen: External audit review 8 (esketamine-trd-madrs, every LOO CI crosses 0) and review 13 (noac-vs-warfarin-af-stroke).

C5.name: Forest plot without per-study whiskers / null line
C5.rule: Every forest plot (ratio and mean-difference scales) must draw each study's 95% CI as a whisker, the pooled diamond, and a vertical null line (1 for ratios, 0 for differences), with the axis on the right scale.

C6.name: Mixed-measure label propagation
C6.rule: When a pool's inputs carry different effect measures (e.g. HR and RR/IRR/OR; result.estmeasure / scale_mixed), the pooled result's label must not propagate a single measure name (e.g. 'pooled HR') to the Overview, Results, Analysis, claim text, GRADE or index; it must say the measures are mixed (or name the canonical class) everywhere the pooled estimate is described.
C6.seen: External audit review 5 (doac-vte-recurrence, R5-1) and review 23 (balanced-crystalloids-vs-saline-mortality).

C7.name: Stale generated or config text
C7.rule: Generated text that was correct for an earlier object state but no longer matches the current review object (e.g. a label taken from topic config rather than the current source/object, a count or name that the object has since changed) must be regenerated from the current object, never kept as stored prose.
C7.seen: Review 14 (sacubitril-valsartan-hfref: stale generated text) and review 20 (spironolactone-hfref-mortality: stale config label on J-EMPHASIS-HF, PMID 28824029).

C8.name: Invented scope restriction (PIONEER-HF)
C8.rule: A harms or scope note must not invent a restriction absent from the protocol object (e.g. 'chronic only'). Scope text must be rendered from ONE scope decision in the protocol object.
C8.seen: Review 14 (sacubitril-valsartan-hfref): a harms note invents a chronic-only restriction for PIONEER-HF that the protocol does not contain.
